name: 7-Zip
description: Archive packing and conversion through the bundled 7-Zip. Reads far more formats than it writes, so rar, iso, cab and the rest can be converted into zip or 7z.

sharedOptions.label: Compression
sharedOptions.description: 0 stores without compressing, 9 is the smallest and slowest.

sharedOptions.label: Convert archives rather than nesting them
sharedOptions.description: On, an archive is unpacked and its contents written in the new format. Off, the archive file itself is put inside the new one.

sharedOptions.label: Password
sharedOptions.description: Encrypts what is written, and unlocks the source if it is already encrypted. Leave empty for none.

sharedOptions.label: Hide the file names too
sharedOptions.description: 7z only. A zip always lists its contents even when they are encrypted.

targets.label: Extract
targets.description: Unpacks into a folder beside the archive, named after it. An archive that already holds a single folder is not nested a second time.

targets.label: 7z
targets.description: Considerably smaller than zip, and the only format here that can hide its file names.

options.label: Solid archive
options.description: Compresses the files as one stream, which is much smaller for many similar files and slower to extract just one.

targets.label: TAR
targets.description: No compression. The plain container Unix tooling expects.

targets.label: Gzip
targets.description: Compresses a single file. Use TAR first for several.

targets.label: Bzip2
targets.description: Compresses a single file, smaller than gzip and slower.

targets.label: XZ
targets.description: Compresses a single file, smaller than bzip2 and slower still.

targets.label: ZIP (always convert)
targets.description: Unpacks the archive and writes its contents as a zip, whatever the Repack option says.

targets.label: 7z (always convert)
targets.description: Unpacks the archive and writes its contents as a 7z, whatever the Repack option says.

targets.label: TAR.GZ
targets.description: A tar compressed with gzip, the usual way to hand files to Linux and macOS.

targets.label: TAR.XZ
targets.description: A tar compressed with xz: smaller than gzip, slower to make.
